# Grafana golden corpus sources

Real-world Grafana dashboards the importer is tested against.
Every file is fetched from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<repository>/<commit>/<path>` at the commit recorded below.
Files are kept byte-for-byte as fetched, except the kube-prometheus entries, which are re-serialized from YAML.
Each source directory carries the upstream `LICENSE`; none of the upstream repositories has a `NOTICE` file.
Dashboards from grafana.com carry no license and are excluded.
Files from the AGPL-3.0 grafana/grafana repository are excluded.
A new corpus file needs a section here and a `LICENSE` in its source directory first.

## slashobserve

- Repository: https://github.com/slashobserve/slashobserve (this repository)
- License: Apache-2.0
- Authored: 2026-10-19
- Files:
  - `demo-shop.json`
  - `panel-types-a.json`
  - `panel-types-b.json`
- `demo-shop.json` is a classic Grafana 11 dashboard authored in this repository for the demo stack.
- It holds one panel of every Grafana panel type SlashObserve supports, in six rows, each backed by demo shop data: Prometheus metrics, and ClickHouse queries over the `otel_logs` and `otel_traces` tables.
- The annotation list and Alertmanager groups panels import as placeholders, because SlashObserve has no annotations or Alertmanager yet.
- The news panel reads the Grafana blog feed, `https://grafana.com/blog/news.xml`, which is the feed Grafana's own news panel shows when no feed URL is set (`DEFAULT_FEED_URL` in `public/app/plugins/panel/news/constants.ts` of grafana/grafana).
- The geomap places each service on an example region with a fixed mapping in its SQL, because the shop reports no location.
- `panel-types-a.json` covers the panel types missing from the upstream corpus.
- `panel-types-b.json` covers the map, canvas, alert list, dashboard list and discrete panel types, with one panel for each case the importer converts; the corpus checks that the Prometheus alert list's query is the one the importer writes.
- The ClickHouse targets set `format` to the sqlds `FormatQueryOption` value: 0 for time series, 1 for table, 2 for logs, 3 for trace.
- The `src/types/` directory of grafana/clickhouse-datasource at the commit above declares no `Format` enum.
- Its `CHQueryBase.format` is a bare `number` whose comment points at `FormatQueryOption` in https://github.com/grafana/sqlds (`query.go`, commit dda2dc0a54b128961fc9f7885baabf555f3ddfdc), which is where the values come from.
- The corpus mostly agrees: time series panels use 0, tables use 1 and logs panels use 2.
- Exceptions exist, so `format` is not a reliable guide to panel type: grafana/clickhouse-datasource has time series targets with format 1 and 2 and a table with 0, and Altinity has a logs panel with 1.

## Panel types in the corpus

Counted over every corpus JSON file: top-level `panels`, nested row `panels`, and legacy `rows[].panels`.
Each legacy `rows[]` entry is also counted as one `row`, although it is a dashboard-level object and not a panel.
Legacy rows occur in these files, with their entry counts: `rfmoz/node-exporter-full-old.json` (19), `thanos/bucket-replicate.json` (2), `thanos/compact.json` (7), `thanos/overview.json` (7), `thanos/query-frontend.json` (3), `thanos/query.json` (7), `thanos/receive.json` (11), `thanos/rule.json` (6), `thanos/sidecar.json` (5), `thanos/store.json` (9).
They account for the gap between 2207 entries and the stated 2283.
The corpus holds 101 dashboards and 2283 panels including rows.
Three files exceed 100 panels including rows: `rfmoz/node-exporter-full-old.json` (191), `rfmoz/node-exporter-full.json` (141), `rfmoz/haproxy.json` (113).
